description:
FILED s473t6d (Opus, 2026-09-20) by #1501 round 11 (CHECK 2 on t/op/eval.t:730-753).

perl: `UNITCHECK { ... }` runs just after the COMPILATION UNIT that contains
it has been compiled -- for a string eval, right after that eval's own
compilation, before it runs.  PCL never runs it; the block's body simply does
not execute.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL):

    perl -e 'eval "UNITCHECK { print q(A-) }"; print "ok"'
    perl: A-ok
    PCL:  ok

ROWS: baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv op/eval.t 149, 150, 151, 152, 163, 164
(the file's "No segfault" set, which asserts the block RAN by printing `A-`).
Rows 163/164 nest it inside `INIT { ... }` and PCL prints `0A-ok` / `ok`.

SHAPE: PCL has BEGIN and END phases (`p-eval-always`, the compile-phase block
runner) and INIT; UNITCHECK is the one phase with no arm.  Its unit is the
FILE for file-level code and the EVAL for `eval STRING`, which is what makes
it different from INIT and what the rows above test.  CHECK is the sibling to
audit at the same time (not measured here).
subject: UNITCHECK blocks are never run (6 rows of t/op/eval.t)
